studies.Title: Fatty Acid Intake and Bladder Cancer Risk: A Multicenter Case-Control Study in Iran.
studies.Authors: Seyyedsalehi MS, Hadji M, Rashidian H, Naghibzadeh-Tahami A, Marzban M, Zendehdel K, Boffetta P

sample_size.excerpt: Data were collected from 711 bladder cancer cases and 3,297 controls in the IROPICAN study (2017-2020) across ten Iranian provinces.
sample_size.location: Abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 711 + 3297 = 4008

cases.excerpt: Data were collected from 711 bladder cancer cases and 3,297 controls in the IROPICAN study (2017-2020) across ten Iranian provinces.

comparison.excerpt: Conversely, OR for high intake of palmitoleic acid, alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), and docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) was elevated.

design.excerpt: Fatty Acid Intake and Bladder Cancer Risk: A Multicenter Case-Control Study in Iran.

timing.excerpt: Data were collected from 711 bladder cancer cases and 3,297 controls in the IROPICAN study (2017-2020) across ten Iranian provinces.

continent.excerpt: Data were collected from 711 bladder cancer cases and 3,297 controls in the IROPICAN study (2017-2020) across ten Iranian provinces.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire.

gender.excerpt: Sex-specific effects were found stearic acid was protective in men, while PUFAs were protective in women.
